readme.note: UI dashboard elements demo. A 'Pricing Calculator' Business Function reads two dashboard inputs — a Numeric Input labeled 'Base Price' and a Text Input labeled 'Discount Code' — and writes two dashboard outputs — a Numeric Output labeled 'Total Cost' and a Text Output labeled 'Status'. None of the four dashboard elements are connected to the Calculator with a line: each one's own 'Bound Part' field (Root Properties) points at the Calculator instead — select any of the four to see it. Step Simulation to run the Calculator's script, which reads ctx.ui.UINumericInput['Base Price']/ctx.ui.UITextInput['Discount Code'] and writes ctx.ui.UINumericOutput['Total Cost']/ctx.ui.UITextOutput['Status'] — the two Output elements' badges update immediately (they're always shown, regardless of the view's own 'Show Left Badge' setting). Try editing the two Input elements' own 'Value' field (Root Properties) — type a new Base Price, or the code SAVE10 for a 10% discount, any other text for an unrecognized-code message, or clear it entirely — then Step again to see the outputs recompute. Also try File > Load Example > Model Copy this whole model into a new one, then bind a second set of dashboard elements to the copy's own Calculator: each model's simulation steps independently, so both sets of badges update on their own.

parts.label: Pricing Calculator
parts.description: Reads the two Input dashboard elements bound to it and writes the two Output dashboard elements bound to it, via ctx.ui — a separate channel from ctx.inputs/connectors entirely.
